newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives say polls show gap narrowing.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives say polls show gap narrowing.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservative Party said on Wednesday that its private opinion polls had shown it trailing the opposition Labour Party by less than 10 points every day in the past week.

"We don't talk about our private polls but I am prepared to confirm that as far as our daily private polls are concerned the gap between the Labour Party and the Conservative Party has been less than 10 percent consistently since last Thursday," Conservative chairman Brian Mawhinney told a news conference.

Mawhinney said worry about Labour's policies on Europe, fears that Labour's would ruin Britain's strong economy, and a growing preference for Prime Minister John Major over Labour leader Tony Blair were the three key factors behind a swing in support back to the Conservative Party.
An ICM poll in Wednesday's Guardian showed Labour's lead had shrunk to five pointS from 14 over the past week.
